coverage_note: Whole file read. Lesson = T-verb review (bakser/bankeser, ba8ayyer/bat8ayyar, basawwer/batsawwar, bazakker/batzakkar) as English-to-Arabic translation drills; Amal's chat lines lag 30-120 s and carry the model sentence. Echo/engine notes: 01:58 'شو كمان مرا' = kaman marra? (again?) - Amal repeats herself, not a slip; 02:04 'ما تفي' = his echo of مطفي (S4); 02:37 'قمت إمني' unreadable engine stretch (meant 'I got up ... drank a lot of coffee and I'm ready'), nothing scorable; 04:00 'خروف is pig' self-fixed to lamb in English; 06:59 'Bara.' is his own Latin barra (away), not an echo of روّح; 10:18 'banzehj' = a guess at which verb was left (not a use); 14:57 كسروا -> انكسروا and 17:13 اكسرو -> ما تكسرو self-fixed before Amal (GR-22, not rows); 24:11 Latin 'Ashan il internet o il ijtema' fine; 26:57 'عطلوا / أتلوا' = 2aatalu with the ق dropped (S4, matches her own spelling 2aatalu) - only the missing بعض is filed; 27:52 'كسا' = cut-off كسر (S5); 28:21 راس الثاني = Amal finished the word he had started (help, not a slip); 32:19 he blanked on طيارة and found it after her 'remember car?' hint (not a row); 39:52 'الآن' = engine for a near-miss of الألوان (Amal 'very close'), pronunciation; 41:43 تنغيّر -> بنغير self-fixed; 48:51 ما تصوري -> ما تتصوري self-fixed; 54:07 engine wrote بيصوّر but Amal said she heard يصور (TR-18: trust her echo) - no slip; 55:46 صوّرتي -> صورْت self-fixed before her word; 58:00 'maqtarakhar' unreadable Latin; 1:04:00 شُكْر = Farsi/pronunciation chat, not Arabic use. Pre-ruled tier-3 let-pass (AR-1933) not seen: his English inside Arabic was always meta ('what's called', 'how to', 'change your flight'). Latin stretches: 06:46, 08:27, 11:46, 24:11, 50:32, 52:15, 58:37-58:54, 1:00:07, 1:02:35, 1:03:04 (all read).

rows.right: على التسعة ونص / الساعة تسعة ونص (my reading)

rows.medi_said: معروف is ground؟ معروف؟ No. ... مرفوف؟ What was What was ground؟

rows.right: لحمة عجل مفرومة (my reading; sheet: la7meh mafrumeh)

خضرة is feminine; he wondered about مختلفة then settled on masculine مختلف and Amal let it pass.

Past 'he came' is إجا (sheet: huwwe aja); he said أجي, Amal recast أجا and he repeated it.
He said 'came FROM my house' meaning 'came TO my house'; Amal recast the preposition (أجا على / أجا عندي) and he repeated أجا على بيتي.

rows.why: Explaining بكسر as 'I make something broken' he used the bare/command form خلّي for 'I make'; the plain present needs b- (بخلي). Amal let it pass.

rows.medi_said: بتكسر. ما بتكسري. ... ما، ما بتس-- بتكس،
rows.chat: e7na benfaddel enno inti ma tekserih
rows.why: 'We prefer you don't break it': after بنفضل the verb loses its b- (and as a don't-command it is ما تكسري); he kept the b- (ما بتكسري), Amal recast ما تكسري and he repeated ما تكسريه.
rows.english: we prefer that you don't break it

rows.why: 'I broke it': he stalled on the object ending (kasart ... to); Amal finished it as كسرته. May be only a pause/restart (S5) - low.
'What broke them' is the doing verb كسر; he used the get-broken form انكسر with an object; Amal recast شو كسرهم and he said 'Oh, that's right. It's inflicting.'

rows.amal_said: تكسري. What's plural of أشي إشي؟ ... تكسري أشياء.

rows.english: since when do you break things?

rows.why: 'Most of her teeth' is idafa أغلب سنانها with no من; he started أغلب من, Amal said no (engine wrote نومن) and he rebuilt without من. Chat a8lab snaanha.
He said سنين (years) for teeth; Amal gave سنان and asked what سنين means, he answered 'year'. Different word, not a plural-pattern slip (sheet: tooth = Sin; furshayet snan).
Plural of كاسة is كاسات (he had just said it at 20:27); he produced كسرات (blended with كسر), Amal recast كاسات and he said 'that's right'.

'I change MY mind' needs the -i owner ending (sheet: Ba8ayyer ra2yi); he said bare راي, Amal recast رأيي and he repeated it.

rows.medi_said: We should... Okay. احنا ان لازم--
rows.amal_said: we just should. we not should have. we
rows.chat: we should change the flight time
rows.why: Engine wrote 'ان لازم'; Amal's 'we just should, not should have' shows he said كان لازم (had to / should have) for plain 'we should'; he dropped it to احنا لازم at 31:30.
After لازم the verb is a bare present (n8ayyer); he used the past غيّرنا, Amal named it ('should change. present. مضارع').
Fixing the tense he kept the b- after لازم (بنغير); Amal recast نغير and he repeated. Same sentence as 0915-25 but a second wrong form she fixed again (not a GR-28 repeat of a fixed line).

rows.amal_said: very close. بس السيارة، السيارة feminine or masculine؟ غيرت.
rows.why: طيارة is feminine so 'my flight changed' is تغيرت; he said masculine تغير, Amal prompted the gender and he fixed to تغيرت.

He said شهر (month) for hair three times; Amal said 'شهر is month, what's hair?' and he gave شعرك. May be a ع->ه pronunciation slip (S4) rather than a word slip, but Amal treated it as the wrong word - medium.

'The meeting day' is idafa يوم الاجتماع with no el- on the first word; he started ليش اليوم, Amal cut in with 'day of the meeting' and he built يوم الاجتماع. He had not finished the phrase, so medium.

Second try at 'I reminded him' with a made-up ending -no; Amal recast zakarto and he repeated زكرته.
'They DIDN'T remember me' needs ما before the verb; he left it out, Amal prompted 'didn't' and he added ما تذكّروني.

Plural of اسم in her usage is أسماء (chat el-asmaa2); he offered the other plural pattern أسامي, Amal answered Asmaa and he took it. أسامي exists in some dialects, so medium.

rows.medi_said: Uh, أسامي, um? ... General names? ... I don't know.
